title: S2a-reducibility and differentiation in Martin-Löf random reals
summary: Solovay reducibility is studied intensively as a tool to compare the approximability and the degree of randomness of left-c.e. reals. By definition, a real is left-c.e. if it has a left-c.e. approximation, that is, it is the limit of an effective nondecreasing sequence of rationals. If reals $α$ and $β$ have left-c.e. approximations $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ and $b_0, b_1, \ldots$, respectively, such that the approximation ratios \[ \frac{α-a_n}{β-b_n} \] are bounded from above by a constant, the real $α$ is Solovay reducible to $β$.
